sources.citation: University of the Philippines Diliman, Department of Linguistics, The Katig Collective. 2024. Language capsule: Agta, Mt. Iriga.
sources.note: No phonology or stress information; notes only that the lexicon has loans from southern Bikol languages such as Rinconada Bikol; cites Ethnologue, Glottolog, Lobel 2013, Nickell 1979 and SIL 1984 wordlists.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Section 3.2.3 'The Agta of Camarines Sur, Bikol: Rinconada Agta, Partido Agta, and East Lake Buhi Agta', pp. 68-72.
sources.note: Nothing for Inagta Rinconada: sec. 3.2.3 gives location, sociolinguistic status, lexical affinities (lexicon resembles Rinconada Bikol) and pronoun/case-marker/demonstrative tables whose forms carry acute accents (e.g. dodoón) but no phonology or stress statement. The only stress passages in the dissertation concern Manide/Inagta Alabat (sec. 8.2.9 'Contrastive accent', p. 259) and Maranao (fn. 3, p. 287: loss of contrastive stress in some Bikol-subgroup members, citing Lobel 2003 on Rinconada Bikol).

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2010. Manide: an undescribed Philippine language. Oceanic Linguistics 49(2): 478-510.
sources.note: Phonology is of Manide only. On the target it says (sec. 1) that Inagta Rinconada, Inagta Partido, Inagta Alabat and Manide have 'none... received any substantial attention in the linguistics literature', and that the Rinconada/Partido Agta language 'is a member of the Bikol subgroup with very few features indicating any pre-Bikol substrata'. Cites Fleischman & Nickell 1979 SIL survey report. Nothing on Inagta Rinconada stress.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Possible non-Austronesian lexical elements in Philippine Negrito languages. Oceanic Linguistics 33(1): 37-72 (ScholarSpace preprint pagination).
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.5 'South Agta' (p. 8): Camarines Sur Agta known only from several SIL wordlists taken near Lake Buhi, 'No morphological or syntactic data is available for these languages.' P. 10 transcription note: 'Where stress has been indicated, it is marked as an acute accent on the stressed vowel.' Appendix A (p. 30) lists four SIL Camarines Sur Agta lists (Rugnot, Lake Buhi; Inagta Sta Niño/Sta Cruz; Inagta San Augustine; Inagta San Ramon). Data items show acute on varying syllables (adíŋ 'fire', áŋas 'forehead', sogbóŋ ~ sógboŋ 'shoulder'); no rule stated.
